# orchestrate

> One entry point, nine subagent-orchestration strategies, for any AI coding agent that reads a SKILL.md. Installs as an agent skill.

orchestrate turns "run this plan with subagents" into a controlled process instead of an improvised
one. Every run starts with Prepare: `scripts/capabilities` inventories the machine's research CLIs
(free or paid, installed or missing), build/test tooling, engines and every skill on disk — including
manual-only skills a model never sees in its list; an unclear request gets an interview in rounds
(numbered questions, a recommended answer each — Matt Pocock's grilling technique); missing tools are
proposed with their install command, never installed unasked; an undecided toolchain gets a scout
(X, GitHub, web, registries; track record over novelty, the faster tool on a tie). Point it at a plan
file, a loose idea or a research question and it picks (or you force) a strategy — staged
sequential cycles, parallel worktree fan-out, hierarchical sub-orchestrator fleets, agent teams,
deterministic workflows, goal/Ralph loops, advisor/executor cost splits, adversarial planning, or
external CLIs (Codex/Grok/Cursor/Antigravity/opencode/Hermes/Kimi/Pi) as workers — then coordinates,
dispatches, and gates the subagent work through it. `/orchestrate` auto-triages when no strategy is
forced: it classifies the kind (build, research, fix, review, content, ops), reads the plan's
dependency graph — concurrency is the default, sequence is a finding: builds go hierarchical across
domains, parallel waves inside one, staged only for a true chain; research runs as parallel source
lanes with a fact-checking final gate — and states why it picked what it picked. A plan resting on an assumption nobody has run in the stack starts with one thin proof task; review rounds converge (dismissals cite evidence, settled findings stay closed, churn goes to replan); workers change only what their task needs and report what they noticed elsewhere. Before the first multi-agent
dispatch it shows the user a flight plan — pasted whole into its reply, since tool output is invisible to them; dispatch refuses until the plan has an outcome — the topology tree with model + reasoning effort per agent,
gates, and an honest budget range — and gates on the user's approval (confirm=off skips the gate,
never the print). Every run has a spine: `.orchestrate/journal.jsonl`, an append-only hash-chained record
written only by the controller; `board` renders it as a live terminal kanban (any host, stdlib
python3) with a priced flight plan, test checks on cards, an attention strip and a resume receipt; `board next` is the controller's one checkpoint call and `board help` a ~900-character index by role.
Workers journal one-line learnings (`board learn`) that reach their team at the next board call, together with any decision recorded since their dispatch; `board memory` renders a run as one project-context record for the next run. At finish `board retro` scores the run (outcome, cost, the Brier calibration of every stated `Confidence:`, the board's own friction) and turns a skill-level finding into a field-report draft the user files against this repo.
Agents talk through the same journal (`board send` / `inbox` / `wait` — information and questions,
capped, delivered on the recipient's next board call), panels vote (a lens that never votes leaves the gate pending), and an external-CLI lane is one
command (`board launch … --after N`: the wrapper sleeps in the shell until its inputs are on disk
and never starts the engine if an input cannot land). `board reap` finds what a lane left running
(servers, watchers) by working directory and stint window, and stops it on request; the finish gate refuses leftovers.
Every journal event records the board release that wrote it; `board version` shows a run's start release and each
release since as a migration line (`none` or `action`). Lane receipts record the model that served them; Claude
lanes run with workflows off. `posture=frontier|balanced|economy` picks a concrete harness · model · effort per role
from a dated model catalog (independent benchmarks, prices, context, effort curves; `docs/research/model-selection/`;
refreshed 2026-10-13 for Claude Haiku 5.5 — the economy Claude-only cheap worker at medium, prompts kept under its 100K price tier; Sol workers at medium). A worker whose plan assumption fails returns DESIGN_CONFLICT instead of a workaround;
the controller routes it to a fresh strongest-tier architect (internal design) or the user (product behavior). Claude Code is the reference
host; the skill is plain Agent Skills format (agentskills.io) with a host-adapter layer
(references/shared-hosts.md), so it runs on Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, opencode, Grok Build,
Hermes, Kimi Code CLI, and Pi too — detecting its host at kickoff and degrading honestly where a
primitive is missing.

## Install

- npm/skills.sh: `npx skills add gabros20/orchestrate-skill -g`
- Clone + installer: `git clone https://github.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill.git && cd orchestrate-skill && ./install.sh codex`
- Codex runtime destination: `${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/orchestrate`

## Docs

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/README.md): overview, install, composition presets, saved aliases, repo map.
- [skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md): the router — command grammar, strategy catalog, universal rules.
- [docs/installation.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/installation.md): step-by-step install and verification.
- [docs/usage.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/usage.md): invocation grammar, dimensions, the journal and board command reference, resuming and upgrading runs.
- [docs/strategies.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/strategies.md): all nine strategies in depth — when to use each, their mechanics.
- [docs/recipes.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/recipes.md): composed dimension recipes and saved aliases.
- [docs/research/foundations.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/research/foundations.md): the evidence and sources behind the design choices.
- [docs/research/token-optimization.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/research/token-optimization.md): research record on token/context/cost optimization for multi-agent orchestration.

## Optional

- [docs/designs/v1.34.0-field-loop.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.34.0-field-loop.md): every run is data — board score, calibration from Confidence: lines, the board's friction log, board retro and field reports.
- [bench/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/bench/README.md): the maintainer bench — tasks with hidden tests, decision replays, paired build comparisons against the previous release, field data by release, the evolve ledger.
- [docs/research/2026-10-skill-rl/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/research/2026-10-skill-rl/README.md): research — SkillOpt and text-space RL, a benchmark and an evolve loop for the skill.
- [docs/designs/v1.33.0-board-truth.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.33.0-board-truth.md): a flight plan the user actually sees (dispatch gate, relay line, --ask), one derivation of what is still open, board next, help by role.
- [docs/designs/v1.32.0-review-convergence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.32.0-review-convergence.md): review rounds that converge (settled findings, churn → replan, evidence-backed dismissal), panels that wait for every lens, proof first, workers in scope.
- [docs/designs/v1.31.0-prepare.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.31.0-prepare.md): prepare before dispatch (clarify rounds, tool inventory, install consent, scout), concurrency by default, research as source lanes.
- [docs/designs/v1.29.0-replan.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.29.0-replan.md): reality over plan — DESIGN_CONFLICT, the architect pass, bounds.
- [docs/designs/v1.27.0-versioning.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.27.0-versioning.md): release stamps, migration lines, the compatibility contract.
- [docs/designs/v1.26.0-reap.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.26.0-reap.md): finding and stopping what a run leaves running.
- [docs/designs/v1.21.0-hardening.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.21.0-hardening.md): what five live multi-agent runs said to fix — dependency failure, read-only lanes, the controller's reliable wait.

- [docs/designs/v1.0.0-initial-architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/orchestrate-skill/main/docs/designs/v1.0.0-initial-architecture.md): implementation design shipped in v1.0.0 — why the skill is shaped the way it is.
- [Visual guide](https://orchestrate-skill.vercel.app): every strategy, dimension, and alias on one page.
